_what_this_is: How big the island is inside Unreal, in centimetres, as measured by Content/Python/measure_ue_island.py. The gate's env.ue_island_measured row reads local_bbox_cm and compares it against the object-space box in Docs/qa/graybox_spec_report.json.
_local_not_world: local_bbox_cm is the MESH's own bounds. The script also records bbox_cm, which is the actor's WORLD axis-aligned box. The gate compares local_bbox_cm only. A world box and an object-space box disagree whenever the island actor is rotated at all, so comparing them would fail a correctly placed island. Actor scale is a separate exact check: a right mesh at 0.1 scale is still a 19 m island to a player.
_why_it_exists: On 2026-10-04 the 180 x 100 plate was applied and verified in the .blend, and env.island_sized went PASS. The FBX Unreal consumes still measured 19.3 x 10.7 and the .uasset had been imported from it five days earlier. Every gate row read the Blender source of truth; none read the artefact the game is built from. A player would have stood on a 19 m island while the report said 180 m.
_status: SEEDED EMPTY. Nobody has run the in-editor measurement yet. local_bbox_cm is null on purpose and the gate reads MISSING, not FAIL - nobody has measured it, which is not the same as it being wrong.
_what_the_gate_now_requires: local_bbox_cm - three finite numbers, not strings, not NaN. JSON accepts the bare literal NaN and comparing it with max() used to silently PASS.
asset - must be SM_IslandTop. A number measured from a different mesh cannot answer the question.
level - must name a .umap that exists under Content/HomeWorld/Maps. A sandbox level is not evidence about the shipping one.
measured_at - must be ISO 8601, and must not predate the SM_IslandTop.fbx export. A record that outlives its export describes the previous geometry.
no actor at non-unit scale. The script reports these as non_unit_scale_actors.
_how_to_fill: 1. Open the level in Unreal and run Content/Python/measure_ue_island.py (Scripting workspace, or execute_python_script via MCP).
2. It writes local_bbox_cm and the rest of this file. It only reads - it spawns nothing and saves no level.
3. Commit what it writes. That file is the only evidence the engine has the plate.
If local_bbox_cm comes back near 1930 x 1070 rather than 18000 x 10000, the asset was
never re-imported. The order that fixes it:
c. re-import the FBX over the existing SM_IslandTop asset
d. re-place the island actor if its transform changed
e. re-run measure_ue_island.py and commit the result
Step (e) is the one that gets skipped, and skipping it is how the plate went
missing for a day with nothing going red.

_units: local_bbox_cm is Unreal centimetres. The gate divides by 100 to compare against Blender metres, states the tolerance in metres so a mistaken conversion is visible rather than silent, and derives the X and Y tolerances independently (2% of each axis, floored at 1 m).
